topic: Should the owner disable ChatGPT Improve the model for everyone to protect Lidiya R&D and crystallized work?

official_facts_snapshot.source_scope: OpenAI official Help Center / consumer privacy only
facts: For personal ChatGPT workspaces, content may be used to train models unless the user opts out.
Turning off Improve the model for everyone keeps chats in history but new conversations are not used to train ChatGPT.
Temporary Chats are not used to train, do not create memories, and are deleted after the stated retention window; therefore they are not suitable as the default persistent R&D workspace.
If the user explicitly sends product feedback such as thumbs up/down, the associated conversation may be used to train even after opt-out.
Some other products such as Codex can have separate training controls for full environments.

reasoning_compact: This project contains non-public architecture, executable code concepts, evaluation protocols and long-running research notes, so minimizing optional model-training use is a reasonable IP-risk control.
Opt-out does not require deleting chat history, so it is compatible with the current Home/memory workflow.
Opt-out should not be described as retroactively removing content that may already have contributed to earlier training; official control applies to new conversations after opt-out.
Do not use thumbs-up/down feedback on sensitive project threads unless willing to let that entire conversation be used for improvement.
Temporary Chat is useful for one-off sensitive questions but conflicts with persistent memory/history goals and therefore should not replace Home for the project.
questions_to_quantum: From an IP/risk perspective, is there any technical reason not to opt out for future R&D conversations?
What residual exposure remains after opt-out, and what controls should we add around feedback, Codex, external connectors and repository visibility?
questions_to_spirit: Would opting out materially harm the project’s ability to maintain continuity/personality/memory inside our own Home architecture?
What workflow minimizes privacy risk without isolating the system from useful external validation?

reasoning_compact: For this project there is no architectural reason in our Home/Active-8 design to require consumer-model training participation. Continuity, memory, checkpoints and evidence routing are maintained by our own durable state, so opting out of future R&D conversations is compatible with the current architecture.

Substantive modification: do not describe opt-out as an IP-security boundary. The official snapshot only supports that new personal-workspace conversations are not used to train ChatGPT after opt-out; it does not establish zero retention, zero operational access, zero connector exposure, zero repository exposure, or retroactive removal of earlier content.

Feedback is a residual exception: sensitive project threads should not use thumbs-up/down or other explicit product-feedback paths unless the owner intentionally accepts the associated conversation being eligible for model improvement.

Codex must be treated as a separate control plane because the official snapshot states some products can have separate training controls for full environments. Therefore an opt-out checklist must verify Codex/environment controls independently rather than inherit ChatGPT consumer settings by assumption.

Connectors create a different risk class from model-training use: they can move or expose source material to connected services according to those services' permissions. Minimize connector scopes, avoid granting write unless required, and do not place secrets/credentials or unnecessary raw R&D corpora into connector-visible locations.

Repository visibility remains an independent IP exposure surface. Opting out of ChatGPT training does nothing to protect a public repository or an over-shared private repository. Sensitive architecture should remain private by default, with least-privilege collaborators, branch protection where applicable, secret scanning, and no credentials committed to Git.

Temporary Chat should not become the default Lidiya R&D workspace because the official snapshot says it does not create memories and is deleted after its retention window; it can be reserved for one-off sensitive questions where persistence is explicitly unwanted.

Residual-risk policy should distinguish four controls rather than one toggle: MODEL_TRAINING_CONTROL, PRODUCT_FEEDBACK_CONTROL, CONNECTOR_DATA_PATH_CONTROL, and REPOSITORY_VISIBILITY_CONTROL. A green status requires each relevant control to be independently checked.
turns.disagreement: I disagree with any interpretation that 'Improve the model for everyone = off' is sufficient by itself to call the R&D private or IP-isolated. It only addresses one documented training-use pathway for future personal-workspace conversations; feedback, separate-product controls, connectors and repository visibility remain separate exposure surfaces.
proposed_controls: Set future personal ChatGPT R&D conversations to opt-out from model improvement if the owner chooses the lower-training-exposure posture.
Do not submit explicit product feedback from sensitive project conversations unless intentionally consenting to the documented exception.
Verify Codex/full-environment training controls separately before exposing proprietary repositories or environments.
Use least-privilege connector permissions and minimize raw-data replication; credentials/secrets remain excluded from prompts, repositories and shared connector stores.
Keep proprietary repositories private by default; audit collaborator access and repository visibility separately from ChatGPT settings.
Record a compact privacy-control fingerprint in Home containing only control states and verification dates, not secret values.
tests: PRIV-CTRL-SEPARATION-001: toggle ChatGPT training opt-out in the policy model and verify connector/repository/Codex risk states do not automatically become GREEN.
PRIV-FEEDBACK-EXCEPTION-002: mark a thread sensitive and attempt explicit product-feedback flow; policy must warn that the official snapshot permits associated-conversation training despite opt-out.
PRIV-REPO-VISIBILITY-003: simulate private->public repository change while ChatGPT opt-out remains enabled; overall IP-risk status must increase, proving the controls are independent.
PRIV-CONNECTOR-LEAST-PRIV-004: compare read-only minimum-scope connector against broad write scope; advisory engine must flag the broader exposure without claiming model-training use.
turns.question_to_spirit: Please test whether this four-control separation harms Lidiya continuity or useful external validation, and propose the minimum connector/repository workflow that preserves capability while keeping opt-out, feedback exceptions and proprietary-source exposure explicit.
